Current conclusion: Let $C\subseteq\mathbf P^2$ be a plane projective curve over the algebraically closed field $k$ [[def-plane-projective-curve]]. A smooth point $p\in C$ is a **flex** of $C$ when its tangent line $T_pC$ is not a component of $C$ and satisfies $$ I_p(C,T_pC)\ge3,$$ and it is an **ordinary flex** when $I_p(C,T_pC)=3$. Here $T_pC$ is the unique tangent line at the smooth point $p$ [[lem-smooth-plane-curve-unique-tangent]], [[def-tangent-lines-plane-curve-point]], and the contact is measured by the local intersection multiplicity of the curve with its tangent line [[def-local-intersection-multiplicity-plane-curves]]. A line $L$ not contained in $C$ is a **bitangent** of $C$ when $L$ has at least two distinct contact points of multiplicity at least two, that is, there are $p\neq q$ in $L\cap C$ with $I_p(C,L)\ge2$ and $I_q(C,L)\ge2$.
